source.title: Catching Crypto Trends; A Tactical Approach for Bitcoin and Altcoins
source.publication: Swiss Finance Institute Research Paper No. 25-80

hypothesis: A diversified ensemble of long-only Donchian breakout horizons captures persistent Bitcoin trends while trailing-channel exits and volatility targeting reduce crash exposure.
entry: For each horizon independently, when the prior completed daily close exceeds the maximum close of the preceding horizon, enter long at the next UTC-day open.
exit: For each active model, trailing stop is max(previous trailing stop, midpoint of preceding-horizon max/min closes); if prior close is below stop, exit at next UTC-day open.
ensemble: Equal-weight the nine model activation states.
volatility_target: 25% annualized using lagged 90-day realized close-to-close volatility; leverage cap 2.0x.
funding: Actual Binance funding cashflows included while exposed.
development_gate: net Sharpe >0.70 and positive total return
success_gate: exploratory OOS net Sharpe >1.0, positive at 2x costs, 2024 and 2025 non-negative, max drawdown <35%, and Sharpe remains >0.8 with one-day extra execution delay
note: No optimization of Donchian horizons; exact nine-horizon ensemble is taken from the published specification.
